title: How to Choose an Exhibition Stand Builder in Dubai | FANN
heading: How to choose an exhibition stand builder in Dubai
description: Compare exhibition stand builders using real project evidence, workshop capability, venue responsibilities and a written scope. A practical checklist from FANN.
intro: Choose a stand builder by checking the work, the team and the written scope against your actual stand allocation. A polished render is useful, but it does not tell you who will fabricate, install or handle changes before the show opens.

sections.heading: Start with the same brief
sections.text: Send every shortlisted builder the same venue, hall, stand number, dimensions, open sides, show date, floor plan and product requirements. Include the current exhibitor manual when available. Comparable inputs make proposals easier to judge.

sections.heading: Ask to see completed work
sections.text: Look for photographs of completed stands, not only concepts. Ask what the contractor designed, fabricated and installed on each reference. Compare layouts and finishes relevant to your project rather than assuming a photograph proves capacity for a different stand.

sections.heading: Understand where production happens
sections.text: Ask who fabricates the stand, where the work is done and who checks the finish before dispatch. FANN has a Dubai office and a production workshop in Umm Al Quwain. You can view real workshop photographs and completed projects before discussing your own scope.

sections.heading: Check the venue responsibilities
sections.text: An independent contractor is not automatically an organiser-appointed contractor. Use the current exhibitor manual to confirm submission deadlines, access windows and technical requirements. Name who prepares and submits drawings, orders venue services and answers organiser queries.

sections.heading: Understand the cost drivers
sections.text: Ask for a price breakdown against the same scope. Stand dimensions, open sides, custom fabrication versus an organiser shell, materials, graphics, furniture, screens and lighting all affect the work. Transport, installation, dismantling and storage should be identified separately. Do not compare proposals until you know what each includes.

sections.heading: Make the design-to-quote steps clear
sections.text: Agree the brief before the concept, then record design feedback and the revision being quoted. Ask which drawings, visuals and changes are included and whether any design work is chargeable. Confirm the design scope and approval point in writing before fabrication; do not assume unlimited revisions or a free design policy.

sections.heading: Check whether a shell-scheme upgrade is enough
sections.text: If the organiser supplies a shell scheme, first confirm its walls, fascia, carpet, power and furniture allowance. Then list only the additions you need, such as wall graphics, a reception counter, seating, screens or lighting. Check fixing and electrical rules in the current exhibitor manual before treating an upgrade as a custom-build project.

sections.heading: Compare scope, not a headline number
sections.text: Check materials, graphics, lighting, furniture, AV, transport, installation and dismantling as separate lines. Mark organiser services, utilities, rigging, cleaning, storage and changes as included, excluded or supplied by others. A lower headline can omit work another proposal includes.

sections.heading: Agree approvals and handover
sections.text: Name one decision-maker on each side. Agree how drawing revisions and changes are approved, what must be confirmed before production, and what the handover includes. Ask for a schedule based on the actual show dates and approval dependencies rather than a generic lead-time promise.

faqs.question: What affects the cost of an exhibition stand?
faqs.answer: Ask for a price breakdown against the same scope. Transport, installation, dismantling and storage should be identified separately. Do not compare proposals until you know what each includes.

faqs.question: What should be agreed before design is quoted?

Ask which drawings, visuals and changes are included and whether any design work is chargeable. Confirm the design scope and approval point in writing before fabrication; do not assume unlimited revisions or a free design policy.

faqs.question: Can I upgrade the organiser shell scheme instead?
faqs.answer: If the organiser supplies a shell scheme, first confirm its walls, fascia, carpet, power and furniture allowance. Then list only the additions you need, such as wall graphics, a reception counter, seating, screens or lighting. Check fixing and electrical rules in the current exhibitor manual before treating an upgrade as a custom-build project.

faqs.question: What should I send to get a stand quote?
faqs.answer: Send the booked venue, hall, stand number, dimensions, open sides and allocation plan. Add your show date, brand files, products and required activities. Share the exhibitor manual when available so responsibilities and deadlines can be checked.

faqs.question: How do I know how many sides are open?
faqs.answer: Use your organiser's allocation plan. An in-line stand has one open side, a corner has two, a peninsula has three and an island has four. Confirm the actual boundary and adjoining stands on the plan rather than judging from a sample image.

faqs.question: Is FANN an official contractor for the venue?
faqs.answer: FANN is an independent exhibition stand design and build contractor. No organiser appointment or venue accreditation is claimed here. The current show manual controls contractor requirements and approval steps for your booking.

faqs.question: Where is FANN's workshop?
faqs.answer: FANN's production workshop is in Umm Al Quwain, with project coordination from its Dubai office. The workshop page shows real photographs of the production space and printing equipment.

faqs.question: Are installation and dismantling included?
faqs.answer: Ask for each to be stated in the proposal. The scope should identify transport, installation, handover checks, dismantling and any storage or return transport separately, including who is responsible for venue access and service orders.
